restoration_note: Chapter 110 is heavily damaged. The teaching describes hidden powers (ϩⲛⲟⲁⲙ) operating within the senses/body of man, sealing imprints daily, with myriads of archons of darkness habitually driven outward into Error and metarrhismos / metallismos (transfer of states). Where the editor has supplied small letter-restorations (ⲣ̄ⲓ, ⲙ, ⲉ, ⲛ, ⲡ, ⲁⲗ, ⲣ, ⲣ, ⲍⲙ ⲡ, ⲧⲁⲗⲗⲓ, ⲁ, ⲩ) these are confirmed by Coptic morphology. A few small lacunae are constrained by the spiritual reading: 'hidden' (ⲍⲏⲡ) for the powers, 'hidden' for the root, and a paired hidden-state for some among the archons. Large gaps (17–18 chars) at sentence interiors and unique 1-char fragments without clear morphological anchor have been left unrestorable rather than guessed.

coptic_restorations.basis: Editor's chapter-number marginal repeat (110) at the body's incipit; standard Kephalaia practice.

3-char gap modifying ϩⲛⲟⲁⲙ 'powers'; the chapter's title and reading turn on hidden powers in the senses (ⲍⲏⲡ from the lexicon, 'hidden'). ⲉⲩⲍⲏⲡ = 'being hidden,' the precise sense the title points at.
Apparatus gives est_chars=0; trace ⲣ̄ⲓ at line-end is the marginal numeral, no fill required.

Same 1-char fragment problem; could be a copular ⲡⲉ or a one-letter word-end, but no constraint singles one out.
4 chars, partial ⲉ at break. The reading places the powers' root in interior/hidden degrees; ⲉⲍⲏⲡ ('it is hidden,' Lycopolitan ⲍⲏⲡ from lexicon) fits length and theme — 'their root is hidden'.
4-char prefix to ϣⲟⲟⲡ ('exist'); would be a relative or auxiliary (ⲛⲉⲧ-, ⲉⲩⲣ̄-, ϣⲁⲣ-), but the surrounding clause is lost so no single fill is constrained.
18 chars, weakly constrained; partial ⲡ at break of ϣⲟⲟⲡ but no formula or parallel pins a fill.

18 chars after 'to the body of the man, n-'; trace ⲛ at break could begin many continuations (ⲛⲥⲉ-, ⲛⲁⲣⲭⲱⲛ, etc.); not constrained enough.
18-char gap after 'a myriad-twenty (= 200,000) seals in it'; the predicate is lost.

Editor's word-final ⲛ in ⲁⲣⲭⲱⲛ 'archons'; confirmed.

17 chars after 'they are chosen, purified, come inward'; predicate of motion (ⲁⲡⲥⲁⲛϩⲟⲩⲛ vel sim.) plausible but not securely fixed.
Partial ⲡⲣ̄ visible; in a list 'voice / speech / X' the third member of inner utterance is ⲡⲣ̄ⲡⲙⲉⲩ(ⲉ) 'remembrance' (lexicon: ⲡⲣⲡⲙⲉⲩⲉ). Lycopolitan often drops final ⲉ; fits the 4-char estimate.

Editor's definite article on ⲍⲁⲣⲕ 'stillness/silence,' parallel to following ⲡⲕⲁⲣⲁⲓ̈ⲧ (the Lord's Stillness from lexicon).
1-char gap after 'his heart'; verb-stem fragment of unknown form.

5 chars before 'of God the Father.' The reading frames this as the discriminative election proper to the Father (ⲥⲱⲧⲡ 'choose out / refine,' lexicon entry). 'The choosing/election of God the Father' suits length and sense; alternative ⲡⲱⲣⲭ ('separation') is one short.
1-char fragment ending the line; cannot be reconciled with the trace ⲟ̄ⲁⲥ at the head of the next line by any single confident reconstruction.
Editor's completion of ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'forth' (lexicon ⲃⲱⲗ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ); confirmed.
6-char gap before 'to the outside, in the Error, in the metarrhismos.' A parallel ⲍⲙ ⲡⲕⲉⲕⲉ would fit thematically but the slot is at clause start; not securely constrained.
Editor's completion of Greek loan ⲡⲙⲉⲧⲁⲣⲣⲓⲥⲙⲟⲥ (μεταρρισμός, lexicon entry); confirmed.
Editor's continuation of ⲡⲙⲉⲧⲁⲣⲣⲓⲥⲙⲟⲥ across the line break; confirmed.
12-char gap marked nicht lesbar in apparatus; no anchor for a confident fill.

Editor's restoration of ⲁ that joins line 16's ⲃⲁⲗ to form ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'forth'; confirmed.

4–5 char gap describing 'some among them' just before the contrast 'others among them whom they conceal.' The reading sets up exactly this contrast: some are exposed, others remain hidden. ⲉⲧⲍⲏⲡ ('that are hidden,' lexicon ⲍⲏⲡ) supplies the hidden-state head matched by §5182's ⲧⲍⲡⲁⲩ 'they conceal them.'
Editor's preposition + article before ⲙⲉⲧⲁⲗⲗⲓⲥⲙⲟⲥ; confirmed by parallel ⲍⲙ̄ ⲡⲙⲉⲧⲁⲣⲣⲓⲥⲙⲟⲥ in §5180.
Editor's completion of Greek loan ⲡⲙⲉⲧⲁⲗⲗⲓⲥⲙⲟⲥ (μεταλλισμός, transmigration of states), continuing into next line's ⲥⲙⲟⲥ; confirmed.
Editor's 3pl object suffix completing ⲉϣⲁⲩⲧⲍⲡⲁⲩ 'whom they habitually conceal them'; confirmed.
